provenance.expert_method:
Where I looked: the outer wall on the left side of the classroom wing, from the Plant Room at the top to the stair at the bottom. There is no north arrow on this sheet, so I took the top of the sheet as north, which makes the left side west.
Scale: only used to check sizes (scale bar, 0 to 20 m).
Method: I went along the wall from north to south and looked at every gap in the black wall.
Window: a gap with thin parallel lines inside it (the glazing). All of them are the same size, ≈1.30 m wide.
Door: a gap with no lines inside and a swing arc outside, ≈0.92 m wide. There are 4, the classrooms' doors to the outside.
The Plant Room opening at the top has zigzag leaves: a louvred double door, not a window. The doors split the windows into groups: 2, 2, 5, 2, 7 = 18.
Decisions: neighbouring windows are separated by solid wall piers (≈0.5 m), so each one counts as a separate window. Glazed doors would count as doors, but there are none here.
Result: 18. Exact count, if west = left side of the sheet.

Rules a machine can reuse:

Direction words ("west facade"): find the north arrow; if there is none, take the top of the sheet as north and say so.
Window symbol on CAD plans: a gap in the wall with thin parallel lines inside (glazing).
Door symbol: a gap with no lines inside, plus a swing arc.
Wall piers between gaps mean separate windows, even when the windows are the same size and close together.
Sanity check: a facade with classrooms behind it always has windows; 0 is not a plausible answer.
